tags.name: Blue Belt
tags.note: Wreck cross-check 2026-10-23. Confirmed by >=2 sources: launched 1950, ~103 m, lost at Sha'ab Suedi ~75 km N of Port Sudan, Toyota vehicle cargo, 2 Dec 1977 (2 sources). Conflicts flagged: loss date 2 vs 6 Dec; cargo count 170/181+6/190; depth 15-85 / 20-90 / top at 56 m; post-2013 position (beyond recreational range / past 60 m, diving not permitted / ~100 m). Builder (Howaldtswerke), tonnage (2,399 GRT) and flag (Saudi) are single-source and omitted. Prior 'hull opening at 36 m' entry route claim removed (not traceable).

tags.name: SS Umbria, Wreck
tags.note: Wreck cross-check 2026-10-23 (Wikipedia + 5 dive/maritime-interest sources). Conflicts flagged in text: length 154.9 (Wikipedia) vs ~153 vs ~150 m; scuttling date 9 vs 10 June 1940; cargo 6,000 t of bombs (Wikipedia) vs 350,000-360,000 bombs/8,600 t total; detonators 600 cases vs 60 boxes; max depth 33-38 m; build year 1911 (launch) vs 1912. Prior text on 'dense schools of sweepers', 'crinoids' and 'kitchen and dining areas accessible' was removed as not traceable. Earlier QA labelled the 360,000-bomb figure a fabrication; it is in fact reported by several dive sources and is now shown as a reported conflict. 10,076 GRT is single-source (Wikipedia).

tags.name: Levanzo Wreck
tags.note: Wreck cross-check 2026-10-23. Corroborated by 2 sources: Italian cargo ship, aground Elba Reef 14 Mar 1923, Genoa-Durban salt/general cargo, upside-down. Single-source (Wannadive) and flagged as such: Orlando/Livorno, launched 1901, 339.6 ft, 3,713 GT, sank 28 Mar 1923 after hawser break. Conflicts: length 103.5 vs ~113 m; tonnage 3,713 vs 3,875; depth stern 22-27 m, max 65/70/82 m; Wikipedia March-1923 shipwreck list has a Levanzo grounded 'off Elba' 16 Mar, sank 3 Apr (Red Sea not stated). Wikipedia has no article on this wreck, so the Wikipedia+dive-source requirement could only be met via the shipwreck list.
